_about: Watchdog rules as data. Adding a rule needs the auditor's signature; weakening or removing one needs the auditor AND the county clerk, and the change itself is a receipt on the public journal. Every rule names the real failure it exists to catch.

rules.why: A DEA agent searched Flock under a local officer's password; the log named the wrong person. A user's key only counts on that user's registered devices.
Flock reason fields filled with 'idk' and 'LMAO'. No open case on the county case list, no search.
A dropdown or one-word reason becomes a rubber stamp.
One user, many plates, one day: the bulk-search pattern.
A single case number used as a skeleton key.

params.list: protected-list-v1 (held by the auditor: shelter staff, judges, officers' families)

rules.why: Stalking an ex-partner or a shelter is the abuse that hurts people most. Any lookup of a protected plate goes straight to the auditor.
One California sheriff shared with 1,000+ entities in 44 states. Sharing outside the council-approved list is a violation.
The same key on two different devices within minutes means the key was copied.
California agencies had a logging law and did 'little to no auditing'. Watch the watchers: no signed auditor review for 7 days is itself a violation.
People leave; their keys must stop working the same day.
